intro: Muslims believe the Qur'an came to one man, Muhammad, over about 23 years. Those years had a shape. First there were quiet years in a trade city called Mecca. Then came hard years, when the city's leaders pushed back. Then a move to a new town, Medina, where a small group became a community with rules, battles, treaties and, at last, a book.

This unit tells that story as Muslims tell it, with the dates marked "about," and with notes on what historians can and cannot check. The Prophet's life is not the Qur'an. But Muslims read the two together. A verse about orphans sounds different when you know the Prophet was one. A verse about peace sounds different when you know a treaty had just been signed.

By the end, you will be able to put the main events in order, name the first Muslims and the two cities, explain what the hijra is and why Muslim years count from it, and tell how, according to tradition, spoken words became a written book.
bigQuestion: How does knowing the story of Muhammad's life help a reader understand the Qur'an?

timeline.t: Muhammad is born in Mecca, as Muslim tradition tells it
In the cave of Hira, Muslims believe, the first words of the Qur'an come
Muhammad begins to teach in public; Quraysh leaders grow angry
Some Muslims go to Abyssinia, where a Christian king protects them
Quraysh boycotts Muhammad's clan for about three years
The Year of Sorrow: Khadijah and Abu Talib die
The hijra: the Muslims move to Yathrib, later called Medina
Battle of Badr; the qibla turns toward Mecca
Battle of the Trench saves Medina
Treaty of Hudaybiyyah brings peace with Quraysh
Muhammad returns to Mecca; the idols leave the Kaaba
Farewell Pilgrimage; Muhammad dies in Medina

words.d: a large family group that lives together and protects its members
the square stone building in Mecca that Muslims believe was first built for the one God
a message that believers say came from God
the Muslim belief that there is only one God
the leading tribe of Mecca, into which Muhammad was born
when a group refuses to trade or deal with someone, to force a change
the move of Muhammad and the Muslims from Mecca to Medina in 622
a building where Muslims gather to pray
the people of Medina who helped and took in the Muslims from Mecca
the direction Muslims face when they pray, toward the Kaaba in Mecca
a written peace agreement between two sides
the leader of the Muslim community after Muhammad; the word means one who comes after

choices: A trade city with a holy place full of idols
A farming town with many wells
test.why: Mecca was a caravan trade city, and its Kaaba held many idols.

test.q: Who does tradition say brought the first words of the Qur'an to Muhammad?
test.why: Muslims believe the angel Jibril (Gabriel) came to Muhammad in the cave of Hira.
Tawhid is the belief in one God, the heart of the Qur'an's message.

test.q: Which of these was among the first Muslims, as tradition tells it?
test.why: Bilal, an enslaved man from Abyssinia, was one of the first Muslims.

test.q: Why did Quraysh leaders oppose the message?
choices: The idols brought money, and the message said the rich would be judged too
They wanted to move to Medina
test.why: The idols drew visitors and wealth. The message put rich and poor on the same footing before God.

test.q: What did the Christian king of Abyssinia do for the Muslims?
choices: Let them stay and protected them
test.why: Tradition says the king heard Surah Maryam recited and refused to send the Muslims back.

choices: A speech at the end of a pilgrimage
The move from Mecca to Medina in 622
test.why: The hijra is the move of the Muslims from Mecca to Medina in 622.

test.q: The Muslim calendar counts years from which event?
test.why: Hijri years, marked AH, begin with the hijra in 622.

choices: The people of Medina who helped the Muslims from Mecca
The scribes who wrote the Qur'an
test.why: Ansar means helpers. They were the people of Medina who took in the newcomers.

choices: The direction Muslims face to pray
A share given to the poor
test.why: The qibla is the direction of prayer. In about 624 it became the Kaaba in Mecca.

test.q: Which battle did the Muslims win in 624?
test.why: At Badr in 624 the smaller Muslim force beat an army from Quraysh.

test.q: What was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
choices: A plan to dig a trench
A peace deal with Quraysh in 628
test.why: In 628 the Muslims and Quraysh signed a peace treaty at Hudaybiyyah.

test.q: What did Muhammad do at the Kaaba in 630?
test.why: When Mecca gave in, Muhammad had the idols removed so the Kaaba was for one God.

test.q: What does the Farewell Sermon say makes a person better?
test.why: Tradition says the sermon taught that only good deeds, not tribe or color, make one person better.

test.q: How do Muslims say the Qur'an became one book?
choices: Muhammad wrote it himself in Mecca
The king of Abyssinia printed it
It was gathered after Muhammad's death and a standard copy was made under Uthman
Each tribe kept its own book
test.why: Tradition says Abu Bakr had it gathered and Uthman had a standard copy made in about 650.

write.prompt: The Qur'an says not to push away the orphan (93:9–10), and it says God made people into nations and tribes so they could know one another (49:13). Pick one of these passages. Tell what it says. Then explain how one event from Muhammad's life, as Muslims tell it, helps a reader understand it.
tips: Name the surah and ayah you are writing about.
Say "Muslims believe" or "tradition says" when you tell what people believe.
Pick one event from Mecca or Medina and tell it in order.
Use words from this unit, like revelation, hijra or qibla.
Describe, do not judge. Your job is to explain, not to say who is right.
